known_beginning.verdict_text: Breached: exactly one key fits the intercepted data, and it decrypts the message.

derivation: Counting register: t = 4 qubits, so the phase is read to 1/16; 15 controlled Grover operators were applied.
Most frequent outcome y = 7 (433/1024 shots) → phase φ = y/2^t = 7/16 = 0.4375.
Our Grover operator is −(2|s⟩⟨s| − I)·Oracle, so its eigenphase is π ± θ with sin²(θ/2) = M/N; hence M = N·cos²(πφ).
Peak reading: M ≈ 16·cos²(π·0.4375) = 0.61.
Also seen: y = 9 (372 shots) → M ≈ 0.61 (the mirror phase 1 − φ: same M).
Also seen: y = 6 (63 shots) → M ≈ 2.34.
Also seen: y = 10 (59 shots) → M ≈ 2.34.
Using every shot: M = 1 explains the histogram best (log-likelihood -1522.2) → accept M = 1.
Rejected M = 3: log-likelihood -3597.9.
Rejected M = 2: log-likelihood -3832.1.
counting.true_matching_keys_note: M counts keys that pass the checks inside the circuit; classical post-filtering with the rest of the known data can only shrink that set.

comparison.wallclock_note: Wall-clock time is not the fair comparison: at these toy sizes the classical brute force finishes in milliseconds, while simulating the quantum circuit on a classical computer takes far longer. The meaningful metric is the number of queries — Grover oracle calls versus classical cipher evaluations — where Grover needs about √N against about N/2. No quantum speed advantage is claimed for these miniature sizes.
comparison.oracle_calls_note: Oracle calls are counted per circuit execution (one shot); shots repeat the circuit only to draw the histogram.

registers.name: key
registers.role: Candidate key: starts as an equal superposition of every possible key, and is the only register we measure.

registers.name: work
registers.role: Scratch nibble: holds the known plaintext block XOR the first round key (AddRoundKey K0), for one known block at a time.

registers.name: sbox
registers.role: Scratch nibble: holds the S-box output for that block, then is compared with the intercepted ciphertext block.

registers.name: match
registers.role: One qubit per known block: set to 1 when the candidate key encrypts that block to the observed ciphertext.

registers.name: flag
registers.role: Phase-kickback qubit in the |-> state: flipping it multiplies a key's amplitude by -1, which is how the oracle 'marks' the right keys.
